newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: UK's Premier would considering raising Ratna stake.
newsitem.headline: UK's Premier would considering raising Ratna stake.

text.p: Britain's Premier Oil is not planning to cut its stake in India's Ratna oil field, but would consider raising the level of its stake, Robin Allan, general manager for the Far East, said on Monday.

"From our point of view it's true to say we are not thinking of decreasing our stake. We would look very seriously at opportunities, on their individual merits, at increasing the stake," Allan told Reuters.
Premier has a 10-percent stake in the field.
Earlier on Monday, a senior company official at India's Essar Oil said the company might sell part of its 50-percent stake once a production sharing contract (PSC) was signed.
The remaining 40 percent in the field is owned by India's state-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corp.
The Essar official said the company had not fixed how much of its stake it might sell.
Premier has been waiting for two years to sign a PSC with the Indian government to exploit the Ratna field.
"We see some potential there," Allan said.
